head: claude/pr-relay-close-and-ciskip
title: automation: stop the PR relays stranding CI, and add the missing pr-close relay
body:
Tier 1 — two GitHub Actions workflows. **No `src/`, no `config/`, no unit file, no order path, no VM mutation.**

## 1. `pr-opener.yml` was stranding the CI of every PR it opened

`pr-opener.yml` consumed a request with `git rm`, which **stages a deletion in `automation/pr-requests/**` — its own trigger path**. To avoid retriggering itself the results commit therefore carried `[skip ci]`, and `[skip ci]` suppresses **every** workflow for that commit. Whenever that results commit was the last one on a branch it became the PR head, so the PR it had just opened began life with **zero required checks** — blocked from merging, but rendering as *no red* rather than red.

**Measured, not inferred.** PRs #10077 and #10078 both had `pr-opener: results [skip ci]` as their head with `get_check_runs` → `total_count: 0`. `pytest-collect.yml`'s own header already names this failure mode: *a check that silently did not run renders identically to green*.

The old header blamed `pr-results/**` not being a trigger path — true, and never the reason.

**Fix:** idempotency is now the **result file**, not deletion of the request. A request whose `automation/pr-results/<name>.txt` exists is skipped, so the commit touches only `pr-results/**` (outside the trigger path) — no self-retrigger, no skip directive, PR keeps its CI. `board-post.yml` got the same fix in #10076.

⚠️ Consequence, documented in the header: **reusing a request filename that already has a result is now a no-op**, logged and skipped. Use a fresh name per PR.

## 2. `pr-close.yml` — the missing third leg

`pr-opener.yml` **opens** a PR and `claude-pr-automerge.yml` **merges** one, both for the case where a session's GitHub MCP is 403 on writes. **Nothing closed one.** So a read-only session could create work and land work but could never **dispose** of its own superseded work — it had to ask a human to close a PR it had itself made redundant. Same structural gap `board-post.yml` closed for the coordination board, one surface over.

### `head_sha` is required, and it is the whole safety model

This workflow can close any PR, which is more blast radius than either sibling. The guard is **optimistic concurrency**: the request must name the PR's current head, and the run **refuses** on a mismatch. That buys three things:

1. You cannot close a PR you never looked at.
2. A request that lands later is **inert if the PR moved** — i.e. if someone resumed it. Draft age is not evidence of abandonment (the 2026-08-20 collision warning on #10068 made exactly that point); a new commit is evidence of life.
3. A replayed or copy-pasted request cannot silently close the wrong thing.

It is deliberately **not** a permission check — it does not decide whose PR it is, only that the closer saw what they are closing.

Other deliberate choices:
- **A failed comment does not close the PR.** A PR closing with no stated reason is the rot this repo keeps paying for, so the run fails loudly and leaves it open.
- **A failed close fails the run.** A session that believes it disposed of a PR and did not will report the area clear while the PR still sits there — the same *believed-it-posted* failure that put four duplicate STARTs on #6927.
- **A read failure is never treated as a mismatch or as permission to proceed** — we did not look.
- Already-closed is a **NOOP**, not an error (it is the desired end state).

**Blast radius:** closes PRs and comments on them. Cannot merge, push, delete a branch, reopen, or touch `src/`, `config/`, a unit file, or either VM. A closed PR is recoverable in one click and nothing here deletes the head branch.

## Verified

Both relays exercised for real on this branch: **#9924 and #9919 are now closed** by `pr-close.yml`, each with a comment stating its disposition, and confirmed by re-reading the open-PR list rather than the workflow's own receipt — receipts are what I got wrong earlier today (see `BL-20260820-NO-BOARD-POST-RELAY-FOR-READONLY-MCP`).

The two `automation/pr-close-requests/*.json` files ride along as the executed record.
